reason: Identity overreach: the text says Christian theology INSISTS the redeeming forces are supernatural operations of the Deity; the theology itself is not identical with those operations.

Paragraph directly states mystical states are 'states of insight into depths of truth unplumbed by the discursive intellect', and james-reports honestly reflects the 'seem to those who experience them' framing.
Direction reversed: the text says self-surrender becomes indispensable to the completion of conversion, not that conversion is indispensable to self-surrender.
James asserts in his own voice that nitrous oxide stimulates the mystical consciousness in an extraordinary degree.
The paragraph reports the Indian tradition that the yogi, by yoga training, enters the condition termed samadhi; james-reports is the correct voice.
James states the codified system of Christian mystical theology has orison or meditation as its basis, in his own expository voice.
Reversed/garbled: conversion consists in the focus of excitement coming to lie permanently within a religious system, not the focus consisting in a lodging of conversion.
Noetic quality is one of James's own defining marks of mystical states, asserted in this paragraph.
The paragraph explicitly distinguishes the volitional type from the self-surrender type of conversion.
Direction reversed: in Starbuck's words the candidate must fall back on the larger Power, not the Power fall back on the candidate.
Saint Teresa's quoted account says the union leaves the soul with a certitude impossible to doubt and 'unshakable' belief; james-quotes-source is correct.
James defines conversion as religious ideas previously peripheral taking a central place, in his own voice.
Wrong object: this paragraph says alcohol stimulates the mystical faculties of human nature; 'consciousness of the cosmos' is Bucke's term from a different paragraph and is conflated in here.
Wrong object: conscious strainings let loose subconscious allies working toward rearrangement, not religious ideas.

The paragraph supports that mystical states carry 'a curious sense of authority for after-time', but 'unshakable-certitude' imports Teresa's stronger term from another passage and overstates this object.
Wrong object: Bucke characterizes cosmic consciousness by consciousness of the cosmos, enlightenment, and moral exaltation; 'volitional type' is a conversion-typology term absent from this paragraph.
Identity overreach: the text says temporary exhaustion 'not infrequently forms part of' the conversion crisis, which is part-of, not identity.
Al-Ghazzali's quoted testimony states Sufi mystical knowledge can be grasped by no study or hearsay but only by transport and ecstasy; james-quotes-source is correct.
Direction reversed: James asserts self-surrender is the vital turning-point of the religious life, not the religious life the turning-point of self-surrender.
Subject and object scrambled: David Brainerd is the experiencer who, after his exhausted inability to pray, saw unspeakable glory; 'temporary-exhaustion' cannot be the subject that experienced it.
